text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You are experiencing uterine tenderness, decreased bowel sounds, and urinary frequency alongside your fever. To confirm if this is postpartum endometritis or a urinary tract infection, please tell me if you have had any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or if you have experienced chills?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; your uncomplicated pregnancy and vaginal delivery align with common risk factors. Given your uterine tenderness, fever, and urinary frequency, have you noticed any foul-smelling lochia or foul-smelling urine? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis

The presence of fever, uterine tenderness, and decreased bowel sounds shortly after a vaginal delivery is classic for this condition, even though the urine culture result shows as "Not Requested" rather than a confirmed negative or positive value.
